punchline: In 1968 Douglas Engelbart ran a live demo from a computer in Menlo Park, and the audience of a thousand gave him a standing ovation.
thirty_sec: On 9 December 1968, at a San Francisco conference, Douglas Engelbart spent ninety minutes showing a thousand computer professionals windows, hypertext, a mouse and shared editing. The computer was in Menlo Park, linked by modems and microwave video. He did not talk about the future; he used it live. Accounts say the audience gave him a standing ovation.
